# An override names the target it implements by that target's node.
# A target's own package writes it unqualified, because the node is the
# package's own declaration -- `[android.platform]` inside android.sngl says
# the package's name twice. A program outside the package writes the qualified
# form, which is how the node reaches it at all.
#
# The bare name used to be refused before it was looked up: the index had to be
# a selector, so a target package could only name itself the long way.

sngl check qualified.sngl
stdout 'qualified.sngl: ok'

# Outside a target package nothing is named `platform`: the identity is the
# package's node, and nothing ambient shares its name any more.
! sngl check bareuser.sngl
stderr 'undefined: platform'

# The family every platform node is a member of is not itself a target.
! sngl check family.sngl
stderr 'not a target identity'

-- qualified.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import html "sngl:platform/html"

component mybox[html.platform]() {
    text(value="html")
}

component mybox node {
    text(value="generic")
}

window #home(title="t") {
    mybox
}
-- bareuser.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import html "sngl:platform/html"

component mybox[platform]() {
    text(value="x")
}

component mybox node {
    text(value="generic")
}

window #home(title="t") {
    mybox
}
-- family.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import build "sngl:build"

component mybox[build.platform]() {
    text(value="x")
}

component mybox node {
    text(value="generic")
}

window #home(title="t") {
    mybox
}
